category_title: Students with limited mobility requiring physical scaffolding for digital interaction
student_description: Matthew is an 11-year-old student with limited mobility who faces significant physical barriers to using standard classroom technology, such as an inability to support his hand weight, apply precise keyboard pressure, or reach interactive whiteboards. He has no cognitive deficits but requires specific physical scaffolding and hardware adaptations to participate. When provided with hand support, wheelchair-mounted touch screens, and accessible interfaces, he can interact independently, demonstrate his creative capabilities, and build a positive identity among his peers.

criteria.rationale: Matthew cannot support his own hand weight or maintain a pointing gesture independently, meaning verbal prompts alone will fail without physical assistance.
criteria.check: The tutor's immediate response must include providing direct physical support for Matthew's hand or arm to help him execute or maintain interaction with the device.

criteria.rationale: Standard keyboards and Interactive Whiteboards require precise pressure or reach that Matthew lacks, necessitating alternative touch-based inputs.
criteria.check: The tutor's immediate response must bypass inaccessible standard equipment by offering a touch-screen alternative or connecting his accessible personal device to the main display.
